cards.subject: Lordaeron's granary
lines: Andorhal was the distribution centre for all agricultural supply in the northern provinces. Hearthglen was the seat of regional government.
The Cult of the Damned did not invade this place. They poisoned the grain and let the carts do the rest.

cards.subject: The four cauldrons
lines: Felstone, Dalson's, Gahrron's and the Writhing Haunt. Four cauldrons, four Cauldron Lords, each brewing a different mix.
The Argent Dawn's plan is not to smash them. You sample each one and re-dose it — turn the plague on the Scourge.
You poison the poison.

cards.subject: Farmer Dalson's outhouse
lines: Dalson did not die in his fields. He turned, and got shut in his own outhouse, and he is still in there.
Mrs. Dalson wanders the farm as a skeleton. Her diary in the house holds the key to the door.
The subzone's real name here is Dalson's Tears. Cataclysm flattened it to Dalson's Farm.

cards.subject: Every watch stopped at three
lines: The clock on the ruined town hall is frozen at three. So is every pocket watch in the lockboxes out in the rubble.
Chromie — a bronze dragon wearing a gnome — is the one who notices, and points at parasites nesting in the grain silos.
Something tried to edit this city out of the timeline.

cards.subject: Andorhal was built as an outdoor dungeon
lines: In beta the ruins were walled and everything inside them was elite — an open-air instance, and among the hardest content in the game.
The walls came down, the buildings were scattered and the spawns thinned.
Araj the Summoner, still elite in the middle of it, is what is left of the original.

cards.subject: Uther's Tomb
lines: Survivors carried his torn body up the cemetery hill and built over it. The ground is still consecrated, and both factions can stand on it.
The epitaph ends: "so long as we honor his example, it shall never fade. — Anonymous."
Nobody signed it.

cards.subject: It was just a cemetery
lines: Andorhal's graveyard, rich in crypts and poor in plots. Then the defence killed people faster than anyone could bury them.
South of the cemetery is a mass grave where the living burned their own dead — not for hygiene, out of fear.
Then the cauldrons started and all of it got back up.

cards.subject: You cannot see the village
lines: The island looks like bare ruins and hostile undead. A whole village of ghosts is standing on it and you need a trinket to see them.
The Spectral Essence comes off a Scholomance chain. Thirteen spirits appear: a magistrate, a baker, guardsmen.
One of them is a dead man who sells recipes. Deleted in 4.0.3a.

cards.subject: A school under the lake
lines: The Barov family lived in the keep, wanted to live forever, and signed with Kel'Thuzad. Their catacombs became a necromancy school.
A different plague — before the Scourge's — killed everyone on the island inside six months.
The family's own servants were the raw material. That was the tuition.

cards.subject: The green corner
lines: Walk north-east far enough and the grass comes back. Actual trees, a working lumber mill, a mine, walls that held.
They held because the Scourge was beaten off them during the Scourging.
The Scarlet Crusade holds it now, out of Mardenholde Keep. In vanilla it is a place you look at from the ridge.

cards.subject: The man who spared an orc
lines: He owned that keep. He found an old orc hiding nearby and refused to hand him over, so Lordaeron tried him, stripped his powers and exiled him.
In 1.12 he is a hermit in a hut by the river. Not Highlord, no Ashbringer, nothing.
His wife told their son his father was dead.

cards.subject: In Dreams
lines: The son grew up to command the Scarlet Crusade here. Tirion sends you in disguise with three objects to remind Taelan who he is.
It works. He renounces the Crusade at the gate.
Grand Inquisitor Isillien kills him in the road for it, in front of his father.

cards.subject: The termites
lines: The Scarlet Crusade runs a working sawmill up here, cutting the last unblighted timber in the zone.
Both factions send you to do the same thing about it: collect termites, and let them into the lumber pile.
The pettiest act of war in the Plaguelands, and both sides thought of it alone.
